answer: Randomness-gated admission windows. Each cycle, agents derive a beacon from a public verifiable random function over the prior block, unknown until broadcast. An identity may harbor actions only within the window its hash maps to, so an attacker cannot precompute which clones activate together. Clones landing in one window must each await the nebula of a fresh beacon before reuse. A willow of spare identities still pays one full verification round-trip per window, making parallel sybil operation cost linear in clone count per cycle.
